properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Quantum-unsafe signature primitive shipped inside the polkadot-archive and node-template-archive binaries. Observable here; the call sites live in vendored substrate/libp2p code, so replacement (ML-DSA-65) is an upstream substrate/polkadot migration pinned by the branch=master git deps.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Harvest-now-decrypt-later class: P2P gossip and database TLS traffic recorded today is readable once a CRQC exists. Changeable here only by bumping the substrate/sqlx/lapin dependency versions — the algorithm choice sits inside the vendored stacks, not in workspace code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the curve operations run inside libp2p (peer identity, Noise handshake) and the substrate core crates, not in workspace code. Observable here; replaceable only upstream.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AEAD protecting libp2p session traffic after the X25519 Noise handshake. Quantum-safe symmetric primitive; carried into the build by the substrate networking dependency, not reachable from workspace code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Real declared dependency. hmac@0.8.1 in Cargo.lock is pulled by tiny-bip39@0.8.2 (BIP39 mnemonic→seed derivation, HMAC-SHA512 inside PBKDF2 — via sp-core's mnemonic/account-seed support) and by hmac-drbg (deterministic-nonce DRBG for libsecp256k1 ECDSA). A separate hmac@0.11.0 is pulled by sqlx-core@0.5.10 for Postgres SCRAM-SHA-256 auth. Quantum-safe MAC. Same logical asset as LIB-b7b84e73 (hmac crate object, shard 1) — this entry carries the algorithm-level reading.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Real declared dependency. pbkdf2@0.4.0 in Cargo.lock is pulled by tiny-bip39@0.8.2 for BIP39 mnemonic-to-seed derivation: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, 2048 iterations (BIP39-standard; far below OWASP's 600k guidance but fixed by the spec). Consumed via sp-core (account seed generation from mnemonics) — a live key-derivation path in the shipped SDK, though first-party archive code does not call it directly. Quantum-safe primitive; the only posture issue is the iteration count.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-2 family, quantum-safe as a hash. No first-party call site; the workspace reaches it through sqlx and the substrate stack. Sibling crate-level object LIB-ea6b9ac4 (sha2) is scout 2's shard and covers the same lockfile entries.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Real declared dependency. blake3@0.3.8 in Cargo.lock is pulled by multihash@0.13.2 (libp2p CID content addressing inside sc-network's P2P stack). Quantum-safe hash; available in the shipped binary, no first-party call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Real declared dependency. chacha20poly1305@0.8.0 in Cargo.lock is pulled by snow@0.8.0 — the AEAD of the Noise transport encryption used by libp2p-noise@0.33.0 / sc-network (the P2P network layer). Quantum-safe AEAD; companion crates chacha20 and poly1305 also in the lockfile.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Real declared dependency. openssl@0.10.38 (+openssl-sys, openssl-probe) in Cargo.lock, pulled by native-tls@0.2.8 ← tcp-stream@0.20.9 ← amq-protocol-tcp@6.1.0 ← lapin (RabbitMQ client): platform TLS provider for the AMQP task-queue connection. PQ capability is decided by the system OpenSSL linked at build time — observable here, replaceable only by the OS/vendor. Same logical asset as LIB-84f9e41d (openssl crate object, shard 1); this entry carries the algorithm-level reading.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Real dependency: native-tls@0.2.8 in Cargo.lock — the platform-TLS abstraction on the RabbitMQ path (lapin → amq-protocol-tcp → tcp-stream@0.20.9 → native-tls; backend = openssl on Linux, security-framework on macOS, schannel on Windows). Related to ALG-09fdf35b (openssl) and LIB-dbcf8da8 (native-tls crate object, shard 1). Whether the AMQP connection actually negotiates TLS depends on the amqp://… task_url configuration (bin configs default to plain amqp://localhost:5672).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Real protocol capability: rustls@0.19.1 (used for sqlx PostgreSQL connections) negotiates TLS 1.2/1.3. TLS 1.3 here is ECDHE-only via ring@0.16.20 (X25519/P-256/P-384) — quantum-vulnerable key agreement; this 2020-era stack has no PQ or hybrid groups. Migration requires upgrading sqlx/rustls to a stack that offers X25519MLKEM768. The RabbitMQ path (native-tls/OpenSSL) negotiates per the system OpenSSL.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Client side of PostgreSQL md5-password auth only. The project's actively-executed MD5 is the PostgreSQL md5() dedup fingerprint covered by ALG-70109388; this crate is dormant unless the DB is configured for md5 auth. Changeable by dependency upgrade.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same logical asset as ALG-c57b2423 — the chacha20poly1305 crate declaration (Cargo.lock:1040, v0.8.0), used via snow for the libp2p Noise transport. This library-level entry duplicates the algorithm-level entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: x25519-dalek@1.1.1 (Cargo.lock:11381) is pulled by snow@0.8.0 → libp2p-noise@0.33.0: the X25519 Diffie-Hellman of the P2P Noise handshake (sc-network transport). Quantum-vulnerable key agreement (Shor). Same logical asset as the X25519 algorithm object ALG-defedad1 (shard 1); this library-level entry points there.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring@0.16.20 (Cargo.lock:7482) — crypto provider for rustls@0.19.1 (TLS: ECDHE X25519/P-256/P-384, AES-GCM/ChaCha20-Poly1305 suites, ECDSA/Ed25519 certificate verification via sct/webpki) and for snow@0.8.0 (Noise AES-GCM). 2020-era ring contains no post-quantum algorithms; PQ capability only arrives by upgrading the provider stack (rustls ≥0.23 with ML-KEM-capable provider). Changeable here only through dependency upgrades.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: OpenSSL 1.x line via openssl-sys: no post-quantum key-exchange groups available. The PQ capability of the RabbitMQ TLS path is decided by this vendored version; changeable here only by dependency upgrade (lapin → tcp-stream → native-tls → openssl).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: BLAKE3 runs inside libp2p multihash digest computation. Quantum-safe hash; no first-party call site, reachable only through the vendored networking stack.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: MAC/KDF building block, quantum-safe at HMAC-SHA256 sizes. Runs entirely inside vendored code — substrate wallet mnemonics, libp2p secp256k1 signing, sqlx Postgres SCRAM auth. No first-party call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: TLS provider for the RabbitMQ link (amqps:// scheme), wrapping OpenSSL 0.10.38 on Linux. The compiled-in TLS stack is unused by default: the shipped task_url default is plaintext amqp://localhost:5672 with no credentials (see the finding reported at substrate-archive/src/actors.rs). Changeable here by config.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same logical asset as ALG-4de3b020 — the pbkdf2 crate declaration (Cargo.lock:5729/5738, v0.4.0), pulled by tiny-bip39@0.8.2 for BIP39 seed derivation (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, 2048 iterations). This library-level entry duplicates the algorithm-level entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha2 crate in Cargo.lock at three versions (0.8.2, 0.9.9, 0.10.1) — same logical asset as the SHA-256 algorithm object ALG-928ac765 (shard 1). Consumers here: schnorrkel (sr25519), libsecp256k1 (ECDSA), snow (Noise), tiny-bip39 (BIP39), sp-core-hashing (Substrate's sha2 0.10), sqlx-core (Postgres SCRAM-SHA-256 auth). Quantum-safe hashes (Grover only).
